commit.message:
Tracker: Belobug at 4 fps, not 5: 77.7%, DexNom back at #1 (owner's correction)

Summary, blocker, the "What changed" line, history top-3 (78.1) and
the EDITOR.md note follow. The blocker keeps the README's 5-7 fps.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.patch:
@@ -86,7 +86,7 @@ These stand until the evidence named here changes. If it has, say what changed i
 - **suri (2026-11-24):** the owner added suri as a private build on hyphennn's victory-fork (`basedOn: ["victory-gta6"]`), working in private. PortWatch confirmed a player moving around Lucia's prologue at about 3 fps, in the same scene as the other builds but with rendering ahead: almost like the retail game. So it has `world` and `playable` 1, `render: 0.8` (owner's value), `fps: 3`, `story: 0`: 61%, which leads the headline. `evidence` is "Confirmed by PortWatch". The avatar (`assets/img/efforts/suri.jpg`) is cropped from a profile picture the owner sent, without any app frame. Keep the values; don't lower them or remove the entry on your own. Report code going public, a measured frame rate or progress past the opening in the summary for the owner.
 - **ZETTROX (2026-11-25):** the owner added ZETTROX on hyphennn's victory-fork. PortWatch verified that it plays from Lucia's prologue into Jason's first mission, "Gone Fishing", where it showed the first kill with a gun in GTA VI on PC. Rendering is poor but it's playable. It went in as a private build the same night, then its code went public as `Zettrox/ztrx` (README credits VIctory and victory-fork; tested on an RTX 3050), so it's now a public entry in the race. Owner's values: `world` and `playable` 1, `story: 0.1` (Prologue cleared, the first build at that step), `render: 0.3`, `fps: 2`, `stability: 0.8` (raised from 0.5 the same night: the owner says it almost never crashes, and its README reports 1 h 30 min+ without a crash): 64.2%, #1 in the race. The avatar (`assets/img/efforts/zettrox.jpg`) is the profile picture the owner sent, cropped square. Keep the values; don't lower them or remove the entry on your own. Report a measured frame rate or progress past Gone Fishing, so the owner can decide on it.
 - **Uilian / VItoriaBr (2026-11-25):** `uiliannn/VItoriaBr` was in `ignored` as a credited VIctory fork. After issue 54 and Uilian's YouTube streams, the owner added it to the race. Owner's values from the stream: `world` and `playable` 1, `story: 0.1` (raised from 0.05 so the card reads "Prologue cleared"), `render: 0.2`, `fps: 4` (max seen), `stability: 0.4` (didn't crash much): 59.6%, just behind hyphennn. Checked on 2026-11-25: its code matched victory-fork at a803c87 except a renamed log line and the shader loop-limit override; its own earlier NVIDIA commits aren't in the current tree. That stays as a blocker. Keep the values; report its own code changes surviving on top of victory-fork, or progress past Gone Fishing.
-- **Belobug (2026-11-25):** the owner added `Belobug/VIctory-Belobug-AMD` (public, GPL-3.0, created 09:41 UTC) to the race at #1. It's a VIctory fork for AMD Radeon on upstream main `8e79c80` plus upstream PRs; its README says no victory-fork or myokex/victory-amd code is in it. Platform (README, keep it on the card): Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64 GB RAM, Windows 11; nothing run on NVIDIA or Intel. Owner's values: `world` and `playable` 1, `story: 0.5` (owner's "gameplay 0.5": playable through missions; the card reads "First act"; asked again, the owner confirmed 0.5 because it looks playable through and through), `render: 0.85` (open world looks like retail shaders), `fps: 3`, `stability: 0.7` (rarely crashes, a bit below ZETTROX): 77.4%. Its README still says "not playable yet" at 3-5 fps, with moving vehicles broken, no distant trees and a constant standing in for ray-traced light; that stays in `blockers`. Keep the values; don't lower them or remove the entry on your own. Report a measured frame rate, others reproducing it on AMD, or how far into the story it really gets. Later that day `fps` went from 3 to 5 at the owner's request; its README then said 5-7 fps (5.4-6.7 standing still, less while driving). That ties it with DexNom at 78%, and the stars tie-break puts Belobug first in the race. The owner also said PortWatch has verified it: `verification: "portwatch"` (a value added for this; the card shows "Verified by PortWatch"), and a `"by": "report"` article `2026-11-25-belobug-way-ahead` says the PortWatch team thinks it's way ahead. Don't set `"portwatch"` on any other entry unless the owner says PortWatch has seen that build running.
+- **Belobug (2026-11-25):** the owner added `Belobug/VIctory-Belobug-AMD` (public, GPL-3.0, created 09:41 UTC) to the race at #1. It's a VIctory fork for AMD Radeon on upstream main `8e79c80` plus upstream PRs; its README says no victory-fork or myokex/victory-amd code is in it. Platform (README, keep it on the card): Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64 GB RAM, Windows 11; nothing run on NVIDIA or Intel. Owner's values: `world` and `playable` 1, `story: 0.5` (owner's "gameplay 0.5": playable through missions; the card reads "First act"; asked again, the owner confirmed 0.5 because it looks playable through and through), `render: 0.85` (open world looks like retail shaders), `fps: 3`, `stability: 0.7` (rarely crashes, a bit below ZETTROX): 77.4%. Its README still says "not playable yet" at 3-5 fps, with moving vehicles broken, no distant trees and a constant standing in for ray-traced light; that stays in `blockers`. Keep the values; don't lower them or remove the entry on your own. Report a measured frame rate, others reproducing it on AMD, or how far into the story it really gets. Later that day the owner set `fps` to 5, then corrected it to 4 (77.7%, just behind DexNom). Its README by then said 5-7 fps (5.4-6.7 standing still, less while driving); keep the owner's 4 and the README's range in the blocker. The owner also said PortWatch has verified it: `verification: "portwatch"` (a value added for this; the card shows "Verified by PortWatch"), and a `"by": "report"` article `2026-11-25-belobug-way-ahead` says the PortWatch team thinks it's way ahead. Don't set `"portwatch"` on any other entry unless the owner says PortWatch has seen that build running.
 - **DexNom (2026-11-25, owner's call):** `DexNom/VIctory` (GitHub fork of VIctory, GPL-3.0, created 12:14 UTC, found by the scout on 4chan /v/) joined the race at #2, `verification: "portwatch"`. It's an AMD Radeon build on ZSlayerHQ's victory-world-runtime, tested on an RX 7900 XTX (its BENCHMARK.md: 3.5-4 fps indoors in Chapter 1's city, wrong interior lighting, ray-traced lighting off by default). The owner says it's at the same point as Belobug with the same progress bars, about 0.5 behind: Belobug's values with `render: 0.81` instead of 0.85 (same "Close to the console" step), 76.9%. Later that day the owner raised `render` to 0.9 because PortWatch saw ray-traced lighting working, which puts DexNom #1 at 78%. The owner called it the first to achieve ray tracing, but hyphennn's card already says his streams showed ray-traced lighting, so the site says "the first AMD build on our board to get it". Its README still calls ray-traced lighting experimental; that stays in `blockers`. The owner reports DexNom runs at about 1 fps with ray tracing on (in its summary and blockers; `fps` stays 3).
 - **Doomsday (2026-11-25, owner's call):** a private group, verified by PortWatch, on `JoshuuDev/victory-amd` (a GitHub fork of `myokex/victory-amd`, not tracked, so `basedOn` is empty and the byline names it). The owner says it has ray-traced lighting at 3-5 fps, almost no crashes and the same story progress as Belobug and DexNom, with rendering a bit behind DexNom's; the phone renders well and the map menu runs faster. Mostly AMD, also works on NVIDIA at lower fps. Values: `story: 0.5`, `render: 0.85`, `fps: 4`, `stability: 0.8` (ZETTROX's value for "almost never crashes"): 78.7%. It leads the headline; DexNom stays #1 in the race. The card links the group's X, `x.com/Stu9ao`, as a `proof` link (private cards show `proof` since this change). The avatar `assets/img/efforts/doomsday.jpg` is the owner's picture, cropped. Keep the values; don't lower them or remove the entry on your own. Its Setup.cmd only builds from source with cargo and adds a Start-menu shortcut; Initialize-FormatTables.ps1 downloads one data file from Marvisak/VIctory at a pinned commit and checks its SHA-256 (read on 2026-11-25). Recheck both scripts if they change, and never link a prebuilt download from it. Keep the values; don't lower them or remove the entry on your own.
 - **A shorter board (2026-11-25, owner's call):** the race now holds only public builds scored at or above XCL (35% that day: Belobug, ZETTROX, hyphennn, Uilian, VIctory, XCL). Everything below XCL went to the watchlist: Xbox2Windows, TuxBox, xbox-emulator, ScarlettX, OpenScarlett (Community Edition), OpenScarlett, scarlett-layer, XValkyrie, AnyXboxX. Keep that rule: a project joins the race only when it passes XCL, and one that falls behind XCL moves to the watchlist. The watchlist and the toolkit start collapsed. The "New candidates" and "Fake downloads" sections are gone from the site; `candidates` and `flagged` stay in tracker.json for your review. Nuked entries (Leonida, americas-recomp) are no longer shown anywhere, but keep them in `efforts`: their repo names stop the scout listing their copies as candidates.
